physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the brain stem, in the medulla, the small knot at the base of the skull where the spine and the brain meet. It is the oldest part of the brain, the part that was there before thinking. It is what keeps the breath going while you sleep, what holds the heartbeat steady while you forget you have one, what raises and lowers the blood without consulting you. It is fitting that the code of pure presence sits here, lower than the mind, in the part of the body that has never once stopped paying attention.

The shadow has a floor here. The skating, the absent stretches, the long unlived mornings, all of it lives upstairs, in the cortex, in the thinking that placed itself between you and the room. The medulla never went anywhere. It was breathing you the whole time. The numbness is not the body's, it is the mind's, sitting on top of a body that is already present.

The climb out is also bodily, and small. The breath deepens by itself. The shoulders come down a finger's width. The eyes soften. You did not decide any of this. Something lower than you decided. That is the gift arriving in its own native dialect, the brain stem doing what it always did, only now you are quiet enough to feel it.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to a single amino acid, Leucine. Leucine is one of the small set of letters the body cannot make for itself. It has to be taken in. Carried across the line of the mouth from outside, broken down, and then used. The body asks for it and waits, and only with it can certain things be built.

There is a teaching in that, and it is the strange one this card has been circling all along. Presence is not a thing you generate. It is not something the mind works its way toward by trying harder. It is received. It arrives from outside the small frame of you. The chemistry says it before any teacher does. The code that ends the long noise of thinking is built on an element the noise did not invent and cannot supply. You take in what you cannot make. You stop, and the world feeds you the thing you were chasing.
